:::{#thm-gd-quadratic-error}
#### The error of gradient descent on a quadratic shrinks geometrically

Let $\matr{S}$ be a $p \times p$
[positive definite matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite)
with [eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvalue) $\eigval_1, \ldots, \eigval_p$,
let $\vecf{c} \in \reals^p$,
and let $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\qform{\matr{S}}{\vx} - \dprod{\vecf{c}}{\vx}$,
whose unique [minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-global-minimizer) is $\vx^* = \matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c}$ (@thm-newton-quadratic).
[Gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent) with a fixed [step length](#def-gradient-descent) $\steplen > 0$
from any $\iterpoint{\vx}{0}$ has [errors](#def-iterate-error) satisfying

$$
\norm{\iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \vx^*} \le \convrate(\steplen)^t\,\norm{\iterpoint{\vx}{0} - \vx^*},
\qquad
\convrate(\steplen) \eqdef \max_{1 \le i \le p} \abs{1 - \steplen\,\eigval_i}.
$$

:::

::: proof

Let $\ve^{(t)} \eqdef \iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \vx^*$ be the [error](#def-iterate-error) at step $t$.
The [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) of $f$ is $\deriv{\vx} f(\vx) = \matr{S}\vx - \vecf{c}$
(see the proof of @thm-newton-quadratic), and $\vecf{c} = \matr{S}\vx^*$, so

$$
\ba
\ve^{(t+1)}
&= \iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \steplen\,(\matr{S}\iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \vecf{c}) - \vx^*
&& \text{(definition of gradient descent)}
\\
&= \iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \steplen\,\matr{S}(\iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \vx^*) - \vx^*
&& \text{(} \vecf{c} = \matr{S}\vx^* \text{)}
\\
&= (\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{S})\,\ve^{(t)}.
&& \text{(collect the terms in } \ve^{(t)} \text{)}
\ea
$$

By [induction](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof-by-induction) on $t$, $\ve^{(t)} = (\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{S})^t\,\ve^{(0)}$.
Write $\matr{S} = \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\tp{\matr{Q}}$
([spectral theorem](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-spectral)).
Then $\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{S} = \matr{Q}(\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{\Eigvals})\tp{\matr{Q}}$
because $\matr{Q}\tp{\matr{Q}} = \matr{I}_p$,
and the $t$th [power](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-power) cancels each inner $\tp{\matr{Q}}\matr{Q} = \matr{I}_p$, so

$$
\ba
\norm{\ve^{(t)}}
&= \norm{\matr{Q}(\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{\Eigvals})^t\tp{\matr{Q}}\ve^{(0)}}
&& \text{(the factorization above)}
\\
&= \norm{(\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{\Eigvals})^t\tp{\matr{Q}}\ve^{(0)}}
&& \text{(orthogonal matrices preserve length)}
\\
&\le \convrate(\steplen)^t\,\norm{\tp{\matr{Q}}\ve^{(0)}}
&& \text{(each coordinate is multiplied by } (1 - \steplen\eigval_i)^t \text{)}
\\
&= \convrate(\steplen)^t\,\norm{\ve^{(0)}}.
&& \text{(orthogonal matrices preserve length)}
\ea
$$

The length-preserving steps apply
[orthogonal matrices preserve length](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-orthogonal-norm).
The [inequality](proof-writing.qmd#def-inequality) holds because $\matr{I}_p - \steplen\,\matr{\Eigvals}$ is diagonal,
so its $t$th power multiplies coordinate $i$ by $(1 - \steplen\,\eigval_i)^t$,
whose [absolute value](algebra.qmd#def-absolute-value) is at most $\convrate(\steplen)^t$.

:::
